gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability and persistent oil price shocks could strain public revenues and private investment, reducing market demand for processed agricultural products.
gen_risks.mitigation: Focus project investments on local food security crops and import-substituting value chains (rice, maize, cassava) that remain resilient during fiscal downturns.
gen_risks.evidence: Since the onset of the oil price shock in the mid-2014, growth declined from 6.3 percent in 2014 to 2.8 percent in 2015.

gen_risks.description: Militancy and regional security challenges in areas like the Niger Delta or North East could disrupt project execution, field visits, and supply chains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate flexible allocation mechanisms to prioritize safer agricultural corridors and implement local community-based monitoring and stakeholder engagement strategies.
gen_risks.evidence: compounded by additional factors including a sharp drop in oil production levels due to militant activities in the Niger Delta region.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate financial documentation and unretired travel advances at FPFMD and state PFMUs could lead to ineligible expenditures or disbursement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce an enhanced accountability framework in the Financial Procedures Manual, conduct risk-based internal audits, and mandate biannual external audit reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: The key issues noted within the PFMUs and FPFMD are unretired advances and inadequate documentation of the eligible expenditures incurred.

gen_risks.description: Weak procurement capacity and lack of standardized tools at the state level could cause procurement bottlenecks, delays, and non-compliance with World Bank guidelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Competitively hire dedicated procurement consultants at the NCO to provide continuous technical support, oversight, and capacity building to State Coordination Offices.
gen_risks.evidence: The procurement capacity is still considered low and most of the states do not have procurement tools in place.

gen_risks.description: Delays in negotiating, authorizing, or executing Subsidiary Agreements between the Federal Government and participating states could postpone project effectiveness and credit disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide early legal support and standardized subsidiary templates during project preparation to expedite state-level execution and legal opinion processing.
gen_risks.evidence: At least one Subsidiary Agreement has been executed on behalf of the Recipient and one Participating State and has been duly authorized or ratified

gen_risks.description: A significant drop in agricultural output prices (greater than 10-20%) could erode profitability, turning net present values negative and threatening enterprise viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal off-take contracts and business alliances, while deploying commodity aggregation and storage facilities to smooth price volatility and prevent distress sales.
gen_risks.evidence: if benefits were reduced by 20 percent for all the crops, the net present values will turn negative while the IRR were also below the cost of capital.

gen_risks.description: Increased use of agro-chemicals and execution of small-scale civil works could pollute soil and water sources, generate waste, and degrade natural resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP), ensuring rigorous screening and environmental audits.
gen_risks.evidence: support to sub-project infrastructure involving small-scale works, and agricultural intensification involving the use of inputs, could potentially have adverse impact on soil, water and vegetation covers.

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition for infrastructure support, aggregation centers, or agribusiness clusters could cause involuntary resettlement or restrict community access to common resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Screen sub-projects using the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) and prepare site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) to ensure fair compensation and livelihood restoration.
gen_risks.evidence: infrastructure investments could result in involuntary re-settlement and land requisition.

gen_risks.description: Extension of utility lines, gas pipelines, or power infrastructure to processing clusters could encroach upon or fragment sensitive natural habitats like swamps and marshes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply strict environmental screening checklists under OP/BP 4.04 to realign infrastructure routes away from critical natural habitats and wetlands.
gen_risks.evidence: installation of gas pipelines might pass through important natural habitats such as swamps and marshes.

gen_risks.description: Prevalence of counterfeit or adulterated seeds, fertilizers, and agro-chemicals could suppress yield gains and damage farmer trust in demonstrated technologies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Partner with regulatory bodies like NASC and FEPSAN to strengthen quality assurance, enforce input standards, and link farmers with accredited agro-dealers.
gen_risks.evidence: quality control of agro-inputs such as seeds, fertilizer and agro-chemicals to address issues of adulteration

gen_risks.description: Socio-cultural constraints and unequal access to land, credit, and technical assets could prevent women and youth from fully participating in empowerment activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ring-fence dedicated sub-component funding for women and youth start-ups, deploy a gender tracker, and provide targeted mentorship and business planning support.
gen_risks.evidence: women in Nigeria, compared with men, have relatively limited access to productive agricultural land, inputs and services.

gen_risks.description: Complex multi-tiered governance involving both federal (NCO) and state (SCO) entities could lead to coordination friction, bureaucratic delays, and inconsistent oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Standardize operational workflows using a comprehensive Project Implementation Manual (PIM) and convene regular National and State Steering Committee meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Project implementation will involve both the federal and state governments.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate funding or lack of defined user ownership could cause common aggregation centers, access roads, and processing utilities to deteriorate post-investment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require clear operational management structures and beneficiary O&M financing arrangements prior to committing project funds for infrastructure construction.
gen_risks.evidence: the project will first establish a management structure and O&M arrangement for each infrastructure before investing in such undertakings.

gen_risks.description: Farmers may resist adopting proposed climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive technologies due to risk aversion or lack of practical familiarity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish hands-on technology demonstration plots, farmer field days, and peer-to-peer knowledge exchanges supported by research institutes and matching grants.

gen_risks.description: Commercial off-takers may breach off-take contracts or exploit weak farmer negotiation capacity, exposing smallholders to market and price risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to formalize clear business alliances, build cooperative negotiation skills, and utilize neutral third-party service providers for contract brokering.
gen_risks.evidence: weak market negotiation ability of small producers vis-à-vis buyers and input providers to obtain better prices

gen_risks.description: Delays in establishing and fully staffing new State Coordination Offices (SCOs) in candidate states will delay disbursement eligibility and project rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing CADP project administrative structures in initial states while fast-tracking staff competitive recruitment in new states like Kogi.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made under Categories (1), (2), and (3) ... unless the concerned Participating State has duly established its SCO

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk has been rated Substantial. Coordination of externally funded projects' responsibilities between the federal and state levels is a complex phenomenon, and incomprehension or misinterpretation at any level can affect the project implementation negatively.
gt_risks.mitigation: A communication strategy, supported by the project, will ensure that transparency is maintained at all levels of project management and implementation, and the participation of beneficiaries remains at the core of the project.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risks are rated Substantial. Falling oil prices have undermined economic growth in the country and remain a major source of risks, which may be exacerbated further by security challenges, natural disasters, and climate change. With reliance on a few primary exports and a relatively undiversified economy, Nigeria remains vulnerable to external demand and price shocks, compounded by pressures from weak fiscal management.
gt_risks.mitigation: The World Bank is in close dialogue with the authorities on the reform program in support of restoring macro-economic resilience and economic growth.

gt_risks.description: Sector Policies and Strategies risk has been rated Substantial. One major risk is frequent changes in the agricultural policy, especially the tariff policy, which would change the economic incentives faced by farmers and the private sector alike. Considering this is a multi-sector project, risk associated with other sector policies (e.g., transport and energy) might also affect implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through a sustained, evidence-based policy dialogue and engagement with the government to ensure sustainability of the reforms in the sector.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design risk has been rated Moderate. The approach for agribusiness partnership proposed by this project has already been successfully implemented under CADP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Lessons learned from both CADP and other similar operations have been incorporated into the project design, which is based on analyses undertaken during preparation and summarized under Annex 2.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk has been rated Substantial. While capacity at the federal level for implementing World Bank-supported agricultural project activities is adequate, there is a risk at state level of insufficient experience, structure, and technical knowhow to manage the new project design features.
gt_risks.mitigation: SCOs' staff will be provided necessary training at the time of launching the project, and newly recruited staff (particularly in Kogi state) will benefit from an induction training program. Coordination challenges will be addressed by Steering Committees at federal and state levels, and a Technical Committee at state level chaired by the Commissioner of Agriculture. NCO and SCO will collaborate with FADAMAIII, RAMP, and GEM where relevant, and the project may contract a third-party service provider to assist states in project execution.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (financial management) is assessed as Substantial. The key risks identified are those of value for money in works/construction contracts and capacity building events; capacity building activities such as training workshops have been identified as having significant fiduciary risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: Additional steps include: (i) all training and workshop activities subject to prior review by the Bank; (ii) activities part of the approved annual work plan; (iii) part of the project training plan; and (iv) compliance with the enhanced accountability framework. A qualified procurement specialist will be selected competitively; goods and consultants' services will be procured in accordance with World Bank anti-fraud/corruption guidelines and procurement guidelines.

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk has been rated Substantial. The Environmental Category assigned to the project is Category B, predicated on the assumption that environmental risks and social impact may not have serious adverse impact of a sensitive or diverse nature; the project may not be engaged in development of heavy infrastructure or acquisition of large expanses of land.
gt_risks.mitigation: An Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) have been prepared and publicly disclosed. Specific Environment and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) will be conducted for each public and private investment once the type of work is determined and precisely located, and a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment will cover all areas and localities in which the project will operate.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholders/Gender risk: there is a risk that women will be disadvantaged in terms of their access to employment and participation in out-growers arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: A detailed gender assessment and tracking for the project will be undertaken with the DFID-supported Gender Filter Trust Fund, in collaboration with the Africa Gender Innovation Lab, and incorporated into the Project Implementation Manual. A substantial part of Component 2 (35% of project funding) will support a Women and Youth Empowerment program, with affirmation of 35 percent female inclusion in all aspects of the project (representation in joint community meetings, jobs, extension agents, facilitators, and agri-business/entrepreneurship development), plus TA and training on business plan preparation, accounting, and financial management for women.
